segments.text: This subject is one connected story, not five unrelated papers: financial accounting records what happened and turns transactions into statements; cost and managerial accounting works out what products, jobs and decisions cost; auditing checks whether reported information is backed by sufficient, appropriate evidence; taxation applies legal rules to income and supplies; and finance asks how money should be raised, invested and valued over time. Each area uses information the others produce, so the papers below build on each other.
